Hi Joe — great questions. Short guidance on redaction and cost: 

Redaction approach (recommended):
- Replace sensitive tokens with canonical placeholders: <EMAIL>, <PHONE>, <ACCOUNT_ID>, <SSN> so the context remains while protecting PII.
- For screenshots or attachments, remove the binary and replace with a short description like "[screenshot of billing page]".
- Please keep conversational context around redacted tokens (i.e., "My email is <EMAIL> and my issue is X") so evals can capture realistic structure.

Cost estimate for eval runs:
- redwood-2.7b-int8: ~0.8x cost relative baseline per token, lower latency; good for broader sweep.
- redwood-7b-quant: ~1.6x cost, better quality on multi-turn and long-context edge cases.
We can provide exact estimate after we sample your token distribution.

Prompt collection tips: 
- Include: common support queries, terse internal shorthand, multi-turn escalations, misspellings, and non-English fragments you see occasionally.
- Mark edge cases with column "risk_level" = high/medium/low and add brief notes on expected behavior (e.g., should escalate, should return account lookup prompt).

I've added the Drive link to a short redaction/template doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD3_prompt-sets (see file "ACME_redaction_guidelines.md").

We’ll kick off an automated eval when you upload. Expect an initial pass report (WPS) and a small set of flagged regressions for manual review.

If the upload timeline holds, we'll aim for a review sync on Tue 6/23. Is that time ok?

Best,
Marissa

Adding a few engineering/quality notes for the eval: 

- Eval template: please ensure each example includes a "context" field (previous turns) and a "prompt" field (what user said). Our eval runner uses this to simulate multi-turn behavior.
- Labeling schema suggestion: id, prompt_text, risk_level, redaction_applied (yes/no), ground_truth_action. This helps for regression tracking across model versions.
- Quality regression concerns: we often see regressions around abbreviated input (e.g., "acct# 12345"), so include 50-75 such abbreviations.
- For the high-risk set, include at least 10 validation examples where the correct behavior is to refuse or escalate — we test classifier/intent fallthroughs.

I'll sync with infra to reserve a small eval allocation for Acme so we can iterate quickly.

-Lukas
